HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. BOLD KOREAN WEBTOON movie still — thick black ink contours, hard cel-shade, glossy graphic highlights. NOT photoreal, NOT oil painting, NOT 3D, NOT Caravaggio. Night. The same timber cell. WIDE, slightly high angle, the figure small in the lower third. ONE device: the dying oil lamp as a single gold disc in a vast ink-black cell. Councillor Sunchung lies on packed earth in PLAIN UNDYED WHITE commoner hemp, very thin, ribs a faint ridge under the cloth, one arm fallen open, eyes half-closed, mouth unfinished — still, not a gore shot, not a standing portrait. FACE AND BEARD ONLY from the attached portrait (elderly white hair, white beard, heavy-lidded). DO NOT wear the vermilion court robe, the black silk cap, or the gold flame. No hat. Hair loose on the dirt. The letter is already gone; the cell is empty except for him and the lamp. The lamp burns down just outside the left of frame and rakes a last gold #c9a24d across the white hemp and the beard — not a glow. A slit of feast-light under the door. Monumental emptiness. Loyal even in stillness. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. EXACTLY one named person. No readable writing. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = seongchung. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces). SUNCHUNG — Look: Elderly Baekje councillor: long white hair falling past the shoulders from under a small black silk cap with a single gold openwork flame-and-phoenix ornament pinned at the FRONT of the cap; full white beard and white moustache; heavy-lidded tired eyes, a deep crease between the brows, sun-weathered skin. Dress: Deep vermilion-red wide-sleeved court robe over a cream crossed inner collar, a dark indigo-blue sash, two carved jade toggles and a long red tassel hanging at the waist. Colour #c9a24d. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
